templates.name: Complement lookup
templates.when: Find a pair satisfying an arithmetic relation in one pass.
notes: Generalises to any invertible relation, not just sums.
If the array is sorted, two pointers beat this on space.

templates.name: Seen-set with early exit
templates.when: Detect whether any element repeats, or whether a value has occurred.
notes: `insert().second` avoids the separate count() lookup.

templates.name: Frequency count over a fixed alphabet
templates.when: Compare or match multisets of characters; count occurrences in a bounded range.
notes: An array beats unordered_map on constant factor and cache behaviour.
Space is genuinely O(1) only because the alphabet is fixed.

templates.name: Prefix sum plus hash map
templates.when: Count or find subarrays whose aggregate equals a target, when values may be negative.
notes: Works for any invertible aggregate: XOR is its own inverse, counts mod m also work.
Products do NOT work - zero has no inverse.
Use this instead of sliding window whenever negatives are possible.

templates.name: Merge sort with a counting hook
templates.when: Guaranteed O(n log n) sort; counting cross-half pairs for free.
notes: For inversions, count inside the merge loop instead: cnt += m - i + 1 when a[j] < a[i].
Stable. O(n) auxiliary space.

templates.name: Two-pointer partition
templates.when: Split an array by a binary predicate in place, O(n) time O(1) space.
notes: Destroys relative order. If stability is required this approach is invalid.
Three classes instead of two -> Dutch National Flag, T-SORT-07.

templates.name: Selection by restricted operation
templates.when: Sort when only a limited operation (prefix reversal, adjacent swap) is permitted.
notes: Ask which algorithm needs only the operations that remain, rather than adapting a favourite.

templates.name: Group by an invariant
templates.when: Elements fall into classes defined by a computed key; solve each class independently.
notes: Anti-diagonals use i + j. The algorithm is about the key, not the geometry.

templates.name: Rank map plus comparator
templates.when: Ordering is defined by external data rather than by the values themselves.
notes: The comparator must be a strict weak ordering. Never return <=.
If values are bounded, counting sort gives O(n + k) instead.

templates.name: Sort then adjacent scan
templates.when: Minimum gaps, closest pairs, duplicate detection.
notes: Proof: for non-adjacent i < j, any k between gives a[k] - a[i] <= a[j] - a[i].

templates.name: Dutch National Flag
templates.when: Partition into exactly three classes in one pass, O(1) space.
notes: Invariant: [0,low) are 0s, [low,mid) are 1s, (high,end) are 2s.
mid does not advance on the 2-swap because the incoming value is unexamined.

templates.name: Quickselect
templates.when: k-th largest or smallest without a full sort. O(n) average.
notes: Recurse into ONE side only - that is what makes it O(n) rather than O(n log n).
A size-k heap is O(n log k) and is the right answer when data does not fit in memory.

templates.name: Binary search on an index
templates.when: Find an element, or the boundary of a monotone predicate, in a sorted array.
notes: Count of x = upperBound(x) - lowerBound(x).
Half-open [l, r) removes almost every off-by-one.

templates.name: Binary search on the answer
templates.when: Minimise/maximise a value where feasibility is monotone. The tell: 'minimum X such that...'
notes: Search the ANSWER space, not the array. n can be 1e9; the answer range is what is bounded.
Get lo and hi right: lo must be feasible-or-below, hi must be feasible.

templates.name: Rotated sorted array
templates.when: Search or find the minimum in a sorted array rotated an unknown amount.
notes: One half is always sorted. Identify it, then test whether the target lies inside it.
With duplicates, a[l]==a[m]==a[r] is ambiguous: shrink both ends and accept O(n) worst case.

templates.name: Binary search on a 2D matrix
templates.when: Row-sorted and column-sorted matrices.
notes: Start at a corner where one direction increases and the other decreases.

templates.name: Opposing two pointers
templates.when: Sorted array: find pairs, maximise an area, or converge on a condition.
notes: Only valid when moving a pointer changes the quantity monotonically.
O(1) space beats hashing when the input is already sorted.

templates.name: k-Sum by sort plus two pointers
templates.when: Find all unique triplets/quadruplets summing to a target.
notes: Sorting is what makes deduplication a skip rather than a set.
4Sum adds one more outer loop; kSum generalises recursively to O(n^(k-1)).

templates.name: Fast and slow pointers
templates.when: Cycle detection, finding the middle, or any value-points-to-value chain.
notes: Why the reset works: meeting point is k steps into the cycle, head is k steps from entry.
Applies to arrays whose values are indices - Find the Duplicate Number, Happy Number.

templates.name: Variable-size sliding window
templates.when: Longest/shortest subarray satisfying a constraint, with non-negative contributions.
notes: Requires monotonicity: extending must move the quantity one way only.
Negatives break it - use prefix sums plus a hash map (T-HASH-04) instead.
Each index enters and leaves once, so it is O(n) despite the inner while.

templates.name: Fixed-size sliding window
templates.when: Best window of exactly size k.
notes: No shrink loop - the window size is constant, so it is one add and one remove.

templates.name: Window with a counter, at most K distinct
templates.when: Constraints on the multiset inside the window.
notes: Erasing the zero-count key is mandatory; otherwise cnt.size() overcounts.
`res += r - l + 1` counts every valid subarray ending at r, not just the longest.

templates.name: Monotonic stack
templates.when: Next/previous greater or smaller element; spans; histogram areas.
notes: Store indices, not values - you almost always need the distance.
Decreasing stack -> next greater. Increasing stack -> next smaller.
A sentinel at the end avoids a separate drain loop.
Circular variants: iterate 2n times using i % n.

templates.name: Monotonic deque
templates.when: Maximum or minimum of every sliding window, in O(n).
notes: Each index is pushed and popped once, so O(n) despite the nested whiles.
A heap gives O(n log k); the deque is strictly better here.

templates.name: Bracket matching
templates.when: Balanced parentheses, expression parsing, nesting depth.
notes: Forgetting the final emptiness test is the classic bug: "(((" would pass.

templates.name: Size-k heap
templates.when: k largest/smallest from a large or streaming input.
notes: The heap is INVERTED relative to intuition: k largest needs a min-heap.
O(n log k) time, O(k) space. Correct when data does not fit in memory.
If it does fit, nth_element is O(n) average and faster.

templates.name: Two heaps for a running median
templates.when: Median or balanced split of a stream.
notes: Invariant: lo.size() == hi.size() or lo.size() == hi.size() + 1.
The push-then-transfer dance is what guarantees every element in lo <= every in hi.

templates.name: k-way merge
templates.when: Merge k sorted sequences; smallest range; k smallest pairs.
notes: O(N log k) where N is total elements. The heap holds one head per list.
This is also how external sorting merges its on-disk runs.

templates.name: Iterative reversal
templates.when: Reverse a list, or a segment of one.
notes: Three pointers, in that order. Losing `nxt` is the universal first bug.

templates.name: Dummy head
templates.when: Any operation that might remove or replace the first node.
notes: Use a dummy whenever the head itself may change. It eliminates a whole class of bugs.

templates.name: Runner offset by k
templates.when: Nth node from the end; splitting a list at a proportion.
notes: Starting both at the dummy makes slow land on the PREDECESSOR, which is what you need.

templates.name: XOR cancellation
templates.when: Find the unpaired element; missing number; constant-space counting.
notes: Commutative and associative, so order never matters.
Breaks when duplicates appear three times - use bit counting mod 3 instead.

templates.name: Bit tricks worth memorising
templates.when: Set, clear, test, count, isolate.
notes: Use 1LL << i when i can reach 31 or beyond - 1 << 31 overflows int.
x & -x relies on two's complement and is the basis of Fenwick trees.

templates.name: Subsets / include-exclude
templates.when: Enumerate all subsets or subsequences.
notes: O(2^n) subsets, each costing O(n) to copy -> O(n * 2^n).
`i > start` not `i > 0`: duplicates are only skipped among siblings, not ancestors.

templates.name: Permutations
templates.when: Enumerate all orderings.
notes: Swap-based permutation is O(1) space beyond recursion but cannot dedupe easily.
For duplicates, sort and use `if (used[i] || (i>0 && a[i]==a[i-1] && !used[i-1])) continue;`

templates.name: Combination sum
templates.when: Choose elements (with or without reuse) hitting a target.
notes: The single difference between Combination Sum I and II is `i` versus `i + 1`.
Sorting enables the `break`, which is the difference between passing and TLE.

templates.name: Grid backtracking
templates.when: Word search, rat in a maze, island paths with revisits allowed.
notes: Marking in place avoids a separate visited array and is O(1) extra space.
The `{0,1,0,-1,0}` direction trick gives all four neighbours from one array.

templates.name: Constraint backtracking
templates.when: N-Queens, Sudoku, graph colouring - place, validate, recurse, undo.
notes: Keep O(1) validity sets (row/col/box bitmasks) instead of rescanning - huge speedup.
Return true immediately on success; do not keep searching.

templates.name: DFS traversals
templates.when: Preorder, inorder, postorder - recursive and iterative.
notes: Inorder on a BST yields sorted order - that single fact solves a dozen problems.
Iterative postorder: do preorder as root-right-left, then reverse.

templates.name: BFS level order
templates.when: Anything phrased per level: views, widths, zigzag, minimum depth.
notes: Capturing `q.size()` before the inner loop is what separates the levels.
Right view = last of each level. Left view = first. Zigzag = reverse alternate levels.

templates.name: Bottom-up return value
templates.when: Height, balance, diameter, max path sum - compute a child value, update a global.
notes: The split between 'answer through this node' and 'value returned upward' is the pattern.
Diameter, max path sum and balanced-check are all this template with different bodies.

templates.name: Construct from traversals
templates.when: Rebuild a tree from preorder+inorder or inorder+postorder.
notes: The hash map turns the O(n) index search into O(1), making the whole build O(n).
Postorder version: consume from the END and build RIGHT before LEFT.

templates.name: BST search and modify
templates.when: Insert, delete, validate, kth smallest - exploit the ordering invariant.
notes: Validation needs a RANGE, not a parent comparison - that is the classic wrong answer.
Use `long` bounds, or a node holding INT_MIN breaks it.
kth smallest = inorder traversal with an early stop at k.

templates.name: Grid DFS / flood fill
templates.when: Islands, regions, enclaves, connected areas in a matrix.
notes: O(m*n): every cell is visited once.
Recursion can overflow on a 1000x1000 all-land grid - use an explicit stack or BFS.
Boundary-first DFS solves Surrounded Regions and Number of Enclaves.

templates.name: BFS shortest path on unweighted graphs
templates.when: Fewest steps, minimum moves, multi-source spread.
notes: BFS gives shortest path ONLY when every edge has the same weight.
Mark visited when ENQUEUING, not when dequeuing, or nodes enter the queue repeatedly.

templates.name: Topological sort (Kahn)
templates.when: Ordering with prerequisites; cycle detection in a directed graph.
notes: The length check IS the cycle detection - no separate pass needed.
Use a priority_queue instead for the lexicographically smallest valid order.
Course Schedule I asks only whether order.size() == n.

templates.name: Dijkstra
templates.when: Shortest path with non-negative weights.
notes: O((V + E) log V). The stale-entry check replaces a decrease-key operation.
FAILS on negative weights - use Bellman-Ford, O(V*E), which also detects negative cycles.
Variants only change the relaxation: max-probability, minimum-effort, k-stops.

templates.name: Disjoint Set Union
templates.when: Connected components, cycle detection in undirected graphs, Kruskal's MST.
notes: Path compression plus union by rank gives O(alpha(n)) per operation - effectively O(1).
`unite` returning false is the cycle test used by Redundant Connection and Kruskal.
For grids, map (i,j) to i*cols + j.

templates.name: Kruskal MST
templates.when: Minimum spanning tree / minimum cost to connect everything.
notes: O(E log E), dominated by the sort.
Prim's is O(E log V) with a heap and is better on dense graphs.

templates.name: Cycle detection in a directed graph (colours)
templates.when: Detect cycles, find safe states, validate a DAG via DFS.
notes: Colour 1 versus 2 is the crux: a visited node is only a cycle if it is on the CURRENT path.
For undirected graphs, track the parent instead and ignore the edge back to it.

templates.name: 1D DP
templates.when: Climbing stairs, house robber, decode ways - state depends on a few previous indices.
notes: Define the state in words first: 'best total considering the first i houses'.
If only the last k states are read, roll the array down to k variables.

templates.name: 2D grid DP
templates.when: Unique paths, minimum path sum, maximal square.
notes: A single rolling row is enough whenever transitions read only up and left.
Obstacles set the cell to 0 or infinity rather than needing a branch.

templates.name: Knapsack / subset sum
templates.when: Partition, target sum, coin change, ones-and-zeroes.
notes: Loop DIRECTION is the entire difference between 0/1 and unbounded. Nothing else changes.
Combinations vs permutations: coin loop outside = combinations, inside = permutations.

templates.name: DP on two strings
templates.when: LCS, edit distance, distinct subsequences, wildcard matching.
notes: dp[i][j] = answer for the first i of a and first j of b. 1-indexed avoids edge cases.
Edit distance: same shape, min of three predecessors plus one.
Longest palindromic subsequence = LCS of s and reverse(s).

templates.name: DP on stocks (state machine)
templates.when: Buy/sell with transaction limits, cooldowns, or fees.
notes: Model it as states (holding / not holding) and transitions, not as a search.
Cooldown adds a third state. A fee is subtracted at the sell transition.
Unlimited transactions collapse to summing every positive daily difference.

templates.name: LIS
templates.when: Longest increasing subsequence, and everything that reduces to it.
notes: `tails` is NOT the actual subsequence - only its length is meaningful.
upper_bound instead of lower_bound gives the longest NON-DECREASING version.
Russian Doll Envelopes: sort by width ascending, height DESCENDING, then LIS on height.

templates.name: Interval / MCM partition DP
templates.when: Burst balloons, matrix chain, min cost to cut a stick, palindrome partitioning II.
notes: O(n^3): n^2 states, each O(n) to fill. Constraints near n <= 500 are the signal.
For Burst Balloons, think of k as the LAST balloon burst in the range - that makes the neighbours well defined.

templates.name: Interval scheduling
templates.when: Maximum non-overlapping intervals; minimum removals; arrow shots.
notes: Sort by END for scheduling. Sort by START for merging. Choosing the key IS the algorithm.
Exchange argument proves it: swapping in the earliest-ending interval never hurts.

templates.name: Interval merging
templates.when: Merge overlapping intervals; insert an interval; find free gaps.
notes: `max` on the merge is required - a later interval may be fully contained.
Use `<` instead of `<=` if touching intervals should NOT merge.

templates.name: Sweep line / difference array
templates.when: Minimum platforms, car pooling, meeting rooms, range updates.
notes: Convert each interval into +1 at the start and -1 at the end, then prefix-sum.
O(n log n) with a map, or O(range) with an array when coordinates are bounded.

templates.name: Reachability greedy
templates.when: Jump game, gas station, minimum refuelling.
notes: Jump II is implicit BFS: curEnd marks the end of the current level.

templates.name: Trie
templates.when: Prefix search, autocomplete, word dictionaries, maximum XOR.
notes: Insert and search are O(L) in the word length, independent of dictionary size.
Space is O(total characters * 26); a map<char,Trie*> is leaner for sparse alphabets.
A BINARY trie over 32 bits solves Maximum XOR by greedily taking the opposite bit.

templates.name: KMP prefix function
templates.when: Substring search in O(n+m); shortest repeating unit; palindrome prefix.
notes: The fallback `len = lps[len-1]` is what keeps it O(n) instead of O(nm).
n - lps[n-1] is the shortest repeating unit length - solves Repeated Substring Pattern.

templates.name: Expand around centre
templates.when: Longest palindromic substring; counting palindromic substrings.
notes: 2n-1 centres: n single characters plus n-1 gaps. Forgetting the even case is the usual bug.
O(n^2) time, O(1) space - beats the O(n^2) space DP. Manacher is O(n) but rarely required.

templates.name: Rolling hash (Rabin-Karp)
templates.when: Substring search, duplicate substring detection, repeated DNA sequences.
notes: ALWAYS verify a hash hit with a real comparison - collisions exist.
Use two independent moduli when verification is too expensive.

templates.name: Prefix sums
templates.when: Range sum queries, subarray aggregates, running totals.
notes: Size n+1 with p[0] = 0 removes every boundary special case.
Use long long - sums of 1e5 values at 1e9 each overflow int.
The 2D formula is inclusion-exclusion; the final +P[r1][c1] adds back the double-subtracted corner.

templates.name: Difference array
templates.when: Many range updates followed by one read pass.
notes: O(1) per update and one O(n) pass at the end, versus O(n) per update naively.
Size the difference array n+1 so `d[r+1]` never goes out of bounds.

templates.name: Digit extraction
templates.when: Reverse, sum digits, count digits, palindrome checks without strings.
notes: Check BEFORE the multiply - after it, the behaviour is already undefined.
7 and 8 come from the last digits of INT_MAX and INT_MIN.

templates.name: Floyd cycle detection on values
templates.when: Happy Number, Find the Duplicate - when a value maps to exactly one successor.
notes: Any deterministic single-successor function forms a rho shape: a tail into a cycle.
O(1) space, versus O(k) for a seen-set.

templates.name: Sieve and factor counting
templates.when: All primes up to n; counting a prime factor across a factorial.
notes: Sieve is O(n log log n). Starting at i*i is safe because smaller multiples are already marked.
Use `n /= 5` iteratively, never pow(5,i) - that overflows and carries float error.

templates.name: Binary exponentiation
templates.when: a^b mod m for huge b; modular inverse when m is prime.
notes: O(log b). The inverse identity is Fermat's little theorem: a^(p-1) = 1 mod p.
10^9+7 is chosen because it is prime, fits in 32 bits, and its square fits in 64.

templates.name: Block counting
templates.when: Locate the nth item in a huge implicit sequence without building it.
notes: Use `n-1` consistently once inside the block so division and modulo both land right.

templates.name: Inclusion-exclusion with clamping
templates.when: Overlapping areas, counting multiples, union sizes.
notes: Clamping at zero replaces an explicit disjointness branch.
Beyond two sets, inclusion-exclusion is exponential - switch to a sweep line.
